title_ru: Осирис — аудит ложных погребений и всех названных мест захоронения
core_result: The classical tradition itself predicts intentionally conflicting burial claims: Isis is said to multiply tomb/effigy claims so Seth/Typhon cannot identify the true tomb. The correct research object is therefore a forked provenance graph, not one linear burial narrative.

named_tomb_claims.claim: Osiris burial ground; Djer tomb later treated as Osiris tomb
Eudoxus via Plutarch says Osiris body lies there
Plutarch says body lies there; Diodorus preserves an alternative Memphis/Philae burial tradition
Plutarch reports it alone contains the true tomb
Diodorus reports an alternative tomb tradition

critical_exception.result: Late Egyptian relic geography links the Mendesian nome with the phallus and spine. Scholarly IFAO synthesis cites Dendera and Brooklyn 47.218.84 for the Mendesian Osiris as male member + spine; Papyrus Jumilhac/Khoiak preserves finding of the phallus. Therefore the Nile/fish branch cannot be treated as the only endpoint.
critical_exception.next_search: Banebdjedet/Osiris vessels, relic containers, temple/necropolis object groups, gold/gilded small objects, sealed/hollow/nested items and conservation/X-ray/CT reports from Mendes-related collections.
critical_exception.claim_ceiling: No literal divine body part has been archaeologically identified.

causal_model.research_use: Treat contradictions as routing information: determine which claims are whole-body tomb claims, which are local relic traditions, and which are late literary explanations.
